preamble: The shift from [ə] to [u] is a form of fortition involving both raising and rounding. While less common than reduction, it occurs in specific environments (labialization) or through the influence of orthography. It is also a regular sound change in Austronesian: Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *ə became u in Cebuano and the other Bisayan languages and in Chamorro.

examples.note: Before labial consonants or certain dagesh-doubled sounds, the schwa acquired rounding.
In careful speech, the initial schwa may be strengthened toward the rounded vowel suggested by the spelling.
Also shows the Philippine *R > g reflex.
Only the first-syllable schwa shows u here; the final-syllable vowel is o.
